AC12 names the only safe\n12\tlocations: `/tmp/eval-runs/`, repo `.dev/eval-runs/`, or a CLI-supplied\n13\t`--output-dir` resolved against the allowlist; everything else MUST be\n14\trejected before any filesystem write.\n15\t\n16\t## Public surface\n17\t\n18\t| Symbol | Kind | Purpose |\n19\t|---|---|---|\n20\t| `resolve_scratch_root(path, *, config=None, output_dir=None) -> Path` | function | Resolve `path` and verify it lives under an allowed root. Carries `path` (original input), `resolved` (absolute form), and `allowed` (resolved allowlist actually used for the check). |\n22\t| `SCRATCH_ROOT_VIOLATION_EXIT_CODE` | int constant | Exit code (= 2) the CLI maps `ScratchRootViolation` to. Matches the loader-error trio (`SCHEMA_ERROR_EXIT_CODE`, `INVALID_EVAL_ID_EXIT_CODE`, `UNRESOLVED_CAPABILITY_EXIT_CODE`). |\n23\t\n24\t## Allowlist policy\n25\t\n26\tThe allowlist is `EvalConfig.allowed_scratch_roots` and ONLY\n27\t`EvalConfig.allowed_scratch_roots`. The candidate path is normalised: `Path(path).expanduser().resolve(strict=False)`.\n45\t   `expanduser()` collapses `~`-prefixed home anchors so they cannot land\n46\t   silently inside a sub-tree that happens to contain `eval-runs`.\n47\t   `resolve(strict=False)` allows the directory not to exist yet (M1\n48\t   exit doctor outline runs do not create the scratch tree).\n49\t2. Each allowlist entry is resolved the same way (`_resolve_prefix`).\n50\t   Relative defaults (`.dev/eval-runs`) anchor against the process CWD,\n51\t   matching the behaviour `HomeIsolation` (T02.06) and the CLI `run`\n52\t   command (M2 T02.16) will see at runtime.\n53\t3. See §OPS-001 Closure below; per-deliverable spec at `artifacts/D-0021/spec.md`.\n- R4 (2026-05-20): DOC-OQ4 closure — D-10 added recording the NOTICE/LICENSE attribution mechanism for the vendored ptytest fork. OQ-4 status flips from OPEN to RESOLVED (M2 entry blocker for T02.01 cleared); per-deliverable spec at `artifacts/D-0024/spec.md`.\n\n---\n\n## D-1: PTY layer — fork ptytest vs build minimal pexpect wrapper\n\n### Context\n\nReal Claude Code is a TTY-based interactive REPL. The eval harness needs a PTY (pseudo-terminal) driver that can spawn it, write to its stdin, read from its stdout/stderr, detect \"prompt ready\" states, kill on timeout, and capture exit codes.\n\n### Options\n\n| Option | Pros | Cons | LOC | Risk |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **A. Fork `brandon-fryslie/ptytest`** | Working Claude Code example already exists in repo. Plugin-free standalone class. Active enough (recent commits). | 1 star / 0 forks → bus-factor real. Includes pytest-fixture machinery we don't need. | ~300 LOC adaptation | LOW (ptytest is small, easy to own) |\n| B. Build minimal `pexpect` wrapper from scratch | Clean ownership, no upstream-drift risk, exactly the API we want. | More code to write, debug, test. We re-derive Claude Code TTY quirks. | ~700 LOC fresh | MEDIUM (pexpect has subtle gotchas) |\n| C. Use `pexpect` directly (no wrapper) | Zero abstraction overhead. | Every eval re-implements spawn/wait/expect_prompt patterns; code duplication. | ~0 LOC harness; +~50 LOC per eval | HIGH (drift across evals) |\n\n### Decision: **A — fork ptytest, vendor under `cli/eval/pty/`, fork-and-own posture.**\n\n### Rationale\n\n1. The fork-research report verified ptytest has a working Claude Code example, which means the hardest TTY edge cases (prompt detection, ANSI escape handling, line-buffered reads) are already solved.\n2. Bus-factor risk is mitigated by **vendoring** (we copy the code in; no runtime pip dependency on the upstream repo). If upstream dies, we have a frozen working copy.\n3. The durable dependency is `pexpect` (2.8k stars, active again at v4.9) — ptytest is just a thin layer on top.\n4. 300 LOC adaptation is ~5x cheaper than 700 LOC fresh build.\n5. Option C (raw pexpect) fails the harness-cleanliness goal — evals should look like assertion code, not PTY plumbing.\n\n### Consequences\n\n- We own a small vendored fork forever. `PROVENANCE.md` documents the fork SHA and our diffs.\n- Quarterly review of upstream `pexpect` releases; resync if security-relevant.\n- A new file at `cli/eval/pty/LICENSE` reproducing upstream MIT terms (license compliance).\n\n---\n\n## D-2: Assertion DSL — adopt `Expect.*` port vs raw assertions\n\n### Context\n\nEach eval needs to verify hook side-effects (file presence, JSONL events, settings.json registrations, exit codes, TTY output). The expression of these assertions can be:\n\n### Options\n\n| Option | Pros | Cons |\n|---|---|---|\n| **A. Port `mcp-eval`'s `Expect.tools.*` DSL idea as Python primitives** | Declarative YAML manifest possible. Reusable across evals. Single place to add new assertion types. Mental-model match with industry pattern. | +~200 LOC for the DSL itself. Some abstraction overhead (declarative → callable). |\n| B. Raw Python `assert` statements in each eval | Lowest abstraction. No new code. | Each eval is more code. Declarative YAML manifest not possible (or only partial). Failure messages are ad-hoc per eval. |\n| C. Use pytest's assertion machinery directly | Free; idiomatic. | Couples harness to pytest, but the harness is NOT pytest-driven (it's a CLI subcommand). |\n\n### Decision: **A — port `Expect.*` DSL, ~200 LOC, no upstream dependency.**\n\n### Rationale\n\n1. The YAML manifest schema (§5 of design-spec) is a hard requirement to keep eval definitions declarative and reviewable. Raw Python assertions can't be expressed in YAML.\n2. A small DSL (~10 method types: `file.exists`, `file.absent`, `jsonl.contains_event`, `jsonl.event_count`, `settings_json.has_registration`, `exit_code.equals`, `stderr.contains`, `stdout.contains`, `duration.less_than`, `duration.greater_than`) covers all 15 evals comfortably.\n3. The mcp-eval API surface is a proven mental model — we steal the ergonomics without taking a dependency on the framework (which has the wrong architecture for our needs).\n4. Failure messages from a typed DSL are uniformly high-quality (the DSL knows its own structure); ad-hoc assertions tend to produce noisy error output.\n5. The DSL has a programmatic escape hatch for parameterized evals that can't be expressed in YAML — so we don't lock ourselves out of complex assertions.\n\n### Consequences\n\n- `cli/eval/expect.py` is a public API surface; changes need backward-compat care once evals are written against it.\n- The YAML schema (`suites/suite.schema.json`) and the DSL must stay in lockstep — `loader.py` translates declarative → callable.\n- Out-of-scope for v1: LLM-judge assertions (mcp-eval has these; we don't need them for hook validation).\n\n---\n\n## D-3: HOME isolation — extend existing `IsolationLayers` vs separate class\n\n### Context\n\n`src/superclaude/cli/sprint/executor.py:107-182` already implements 4-layer per-subprocess isolation (`CLAUDE_WORK_DIR`, `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES`, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DIR`, `CLAUDE_SETTINGS_DIR`). The eval harness needs a 5th layer: `HOME` override (and `XDG_*` companions). Question: extend the existing class or build a new one?\n\n### Options\n\n| Option | Pros | Cons |\n|---|---|---|\n| **A. Compose `IsolationLayers` in a new `HomeIsolation` class** | Reuses 4 existing layers for free. No risk to sprint's existing usage. New `HOME` layer lives in eval code, not sprint code. | Two classes to maintain. Slight indirection. |\n| B. Add `HOME` layer to `IsolationLayers` directly (modify sprint code) | One unified class. Sprint also benefits from HOME isolation (theoretical future use). | Modifies code outside this release's scope. Sprint doesn't currently need HOME isolation, so YAGNI risk. The guard fails closed: any of three independent checks raising surfaces a `HomeContainmentViolation`; the partial per-eval HOME is left on disk so the NFR-ISO2 atomic-setup wrapper (T02.13) can tag it as `setup_failed` for forensic inspection.\n\n## Public API\n\n### `HomeContainmentViolation(Exception)`\n\nSingle hard-failure exception type. Callers may catch the base class; branching on the underlying cause is forensics-only.\n\n| Field | Type | Source |\n|---|---|---|\n| `check` | `str` | One of `\"eval_id\"`, `\"scratch_root_allowlist\"`, `\"home_path_resolution\"`, `\"home_path_escape\"`. Lets reporters bucket failures without parsing the message. |\n| `home_path` | `Path` | Verbatim input (no resolution). |\n| `scratch_root` | `Path` | Verbatim input. |\n| `eval_id` | `object` | Verbatim input (`repr`-rendered); non-string scalars stay visible. |\n| `detail` | `str` | Human-readable one-line cause. |\n\n`__cause__` carries the underlying `InvalidEvalId`, `ScratchRootViolation`, or `FileNotFoundError` (chained via `raise ... from`).\n\n### `containment_guard(home_path, scratch_root, eval_id, *, config: EvalConfig) -> None`\n\nThree checks run in order. First failure short-circuits:\n\n1. **eval_id regex (loader-bypass defense)** — re-applies `validate_eval_id` (T01.05) so a caller that bypassed `SuiteLoader` (programmatic test, future REPL) still hard-fails. Raises `HomeContainmentViolation(check=\"eval_id\", ..., __cause__=InvalidEvalId)`.\n2. **Scratch-root allowlist (AC12)** — re-routes through `resolve_scratch_root(scratch_root, config=config)`. Catches a scratch root that is a symlink to a non-allowlisted target (the helper resolves with `strict=False` so symlinks collapse). The allowlist is sourced exclusively from `config.allowed_scratch_roots`; the guard **refuses to synthesize a fallback** (NFR-SEC2 — see \"Bypass surface closed\" below). Raises `HomeContainmentViolation(check=\"scratch_root_allowlist\", ..., __cause__=ScratchRootViolation)`.\n3. **Post-mkdtemp symlink-resolved containment** — `home_path.resolve(strict=True)` collapses every symlink component and forces the HOME to exist on disk; the resolved form must equal or live beneath the resolved `scratch_root`. Raises `HomeContainmentViolation(check=\"home_path_resolution\", ..., __cause__=FileNotFoundError)` when the HOME has not been materialized, or `check=\"home_path_escape\"` when the resolved form is outside `scratch_root`.\n\n### `HomeIsolation.setup(*, config: EvalConfig) -> Path`\n\nIntegrates the guard:\n\n1. Raises `RuntimeError` if `setup` was already called on this instance and `teardown` has not run since (idempotency rule preserved from T02.07).\n2. `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` on `self.home_root` so the scratch root exists.\n3. `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=f\"{eval_id}-\", dir=str(self.home_root))` mints the per-eval HOME. The path is stored on the private `_home_path` slot via `object.__setattr__`.\n4. **`containment_guard(home_path=home, scratch_root=self.home_root, eval_id=self.eval_id, config=config)`** — the FR-ISO2 check runs here, AFTER the slot is populated, BEFORE return. Any failure surfaces verbatim; the slot stays populated so the NFR-ISO2 wrapper (T02.13) can find the partial HOME.\n\n`config` is a required keyword-only argument. No default. No fallback. See \"Bypass surface closed\".\n\n## Bypass surface closed (NFR-SEC2)\n\nA predecessor draft of `setup()` accepted `config: EvalConfig | None = None` and, when `None`, synthesized:\n\n```python\nEvalConfig(\n    allowed_scratch_roots=(self.home_root, *EvalConfig().allowed_scratch_roots),\n)\n```\n\nThe quality-engineer review flagged this as a security bypass: `HomeIsolation.__post_init__` validates `eval_id` (FR-SCH2) but does NOT validate `home_root`, so a caller could construct `HomeIsolation(eval_id=\"E1\", home_root=Path(\"/home/user/.claude\"), session_id=\"x\")` and have `setup()` quietly inject `/home/user/.claude` into the allowlist before invoking the guard. Check 2 would then pass trivially against an attacker-controlled root.\n\nThe fix landed in this deliverable:\n\n- `containment_guard`'s `config` parameter is required (no `None` default, no inline `EvalConfig()` fabrication).\n- `HomeIsolation.setup`'s `config` parameter is required.\n- The home_root-injection fallback is deleted.\n\nRefusal-before-side-effects is preserved: a caller who omits `config` triggers Python's argument-binding `TypeError` BEFORE `setup`'s body executes, so the `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` on `self.home_root` and the `mkdtemp` call never run. Asserted by `test_setup_requires_explicit_config` (assertion: `not any(scratch_root.iterdir())` after the `TypeError`).\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n| AC | Source | Verified by |\n|---|---|---|\n| `containment_guard` raises on FR-SCH2-rejected eval_id | T02.08 AC | `TestEvalIdReValidation.test_raises_on_unsafe_eval_id` (10 parametrized cases) |\n| `containment_guard` raises on non-string eval_id | NFR-SEC2 | `TestEvalIdReValidation.test_non_string_eval_id_is_rejected` (12 parametrized cases: int, bool, None, Path, bytes, list, dict, tuple, float) |\n| `containment_guard` raises when First failure short-circuits:\n\n1. **eval_id regex (loader-bypass defense)** — re-applies `validate_eval_id` (T01.05) so a caller that bypassed `SuiteLoader` (programmatic test, future REPL) still hard-fails. The path is stored on the private `_home_path` slot via `object.__setattr__`.\n4. **`containment_guard(home_path=home, scratch_root=self.home_root, eval_id=self.eval_id, config=config)`** — the FR-ISO2 check runs here, AFTER the slot is populated, BEFORE return. Any failure surfaces verbatim; the slot stays populated so the NFR-ISO2 wrapper (T02.13) can find the partial HOME.\n\n`config` is a required keyword-only argument. No default. No fallback. See \"Bypass surface closed\".\n\n## Bypass surface closed (NFR-SEC2)\n\nA predecessor draft of `setup()` accepted `config: EvalConfig | None = None` and, when `None`, synthesized:\n\n```python\nEvalConfig(\n    allowed_scratch_roots=(self.home_root, *EvalConfig().allowed_scratch_roots),\n)\n```\n\nThe quality-engineer review flagged this as a security bypass: `HomeIsolation.__post_init__` validates `eval_id` (FR-SCH2) but does NOT validate `home_root`, so a caller could construct `HomeIsolation(eval_id=\"E1\", home_root=Path(\"/home/user/.claude\"), session_id=\"x\")` and have `setup()` quietly inject `/home/user/.claude` into the allowlist before invoking the guard. Check 2 would then pass trivially against an attacker-controlled root.\n\nThe fix landed in this deliverable:\n\n- `containment_guard`'s `config` parameter is required (no `None` default, no inline `EvalConfig()` fabrication).\n- `HomeIsolation.setup`'s `config` parameter is required.\n- The home_root-injection fallback is deleted.\n\nRefusal-before-side-effects is preserved: a caller who omits `config` triggers Python's argument-binding `TypeError` BEFORE `setup`'s body executes, so the `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` on `self.home_root` and the `mkdtemp` call never run. Asserted by `test_setup_requires_explicit_config` (assertion: `not any(scratch_root.iterdir())` after the `TypeError`).\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n| AC | Source | Verified by |\n|---|---|---|\n| Why three layered checks, not one consolidated check\n\nEach check defends a distinct attack vector with a distinct underlying primitive:\n\n- **Check 1 (eval_id regex)** defends loader-bypass. The loader (T01.07) validates eval_ids pre- and post-expand, but a programmatic caller can construct `HomeIsolation` directly. The re-validation closes that.\n- **Check 2 (scratch-root allowlist)** defends AC12 policy. The allowlist is a per-run policy concept; `resolve_scratch_root` is the single source of truth and the guard funnels through it.\n- **Check 3 (post-mkdtemp symlink resolution)** defends an attack where the textual prefix passes but a symlink component routes the path outside `scratch_root` at runtime. Only `Path.resolve(strict=True)` catches this — `is_relative_to` on un-resolved paths does not.\n\nConsolidating the checks (e.g., a single regex-validated `resolve_scratch_root` for both `home_path` and `scratch_root`) would lose the distinct `check` identifier on the exception, making forensic bucketing harder.\n\n### 2. Why `config` is required (and not synthesized)\n\nThe initial draft accepted `config: EvalConfig | None = None` in both `containment_guard` and `HomeIsolation.setup`. When `None`, `setup` synthesized `EvalConfig(allowed_scratch_roots=(self.home_root, *EvalConfig().allowed_scratch_roots))` — the rationale was \"the upstream caller validated `home_root` via `resolve_scratch_root` at the CLI boundary, so trust it here.\"\n\nThe quality-engineer review correctly flagged this as a bypass: `HomeIsolation.__post_init__` re-validates `eval_id` but does NOT validate `home_root`. A caller constructing `HomeIsolation(eval_id=\"E1\", home_root=Path(\"/home/user/.claude\"), session_id=\"x\")` would pass check 2 trivially because `home_root` is in the synthesized allowlist.\n\nTwo options were considered:\n\n| Option | Adopted | Reason |\n|---|---|---|\n| Validate `home_root` against the default `EvalConfig.allowed_scratch_roots` in `__post_init__` | No | Would block tests using `tmp_path`-derived scratch roots; would require either monkey-patching the default or adding a 5th field to DM-006 (schema change). |\n| Remove the fallback; make `config` required | **Yes** | Aligns with production wiring (orchestrator T03.16 always passes an explicit config); tests now build an `EvalConfig` whose allowlist matches their scratch root, mirroring production. |\n\nThe adopted option makes `config=None` impossible: a missing argument is now a `TypeError` at argument-binding time, before any filesystem operation in `setup` runs. This is the strongest form of \"refusal before side effects.\"\n\n### 3. Ordering: mkdtemp first, guard second\n\nThe guard MUST observe the freshly created HOME because check 3 uses `Path.resolve(strict=True)` which raises `FileNotFoundError` for nonexistent paths. The ordering is pinned by:\n\n- `test_setup_runs_containment_guard_after_mkdtemp` — spies on `containment_guard` and asserts `home_path.exists()` is `True` at call time.\n- `TestSymlinkResolvedContainment.test_raises_when_home_path_not_created` — confirms the failure mode when the guard runs ahead of mkdtemp.\n\nThis ordering also means a check 2 failure (allowlist) happens AFTER mkdtemp ran but BEFORE check 3, leaving the partial HOME on disk. `test_setup_failure_preserves_partial_home` pins this so the NFR-ISO2 atomic-setup wrapper (T02.13) can find and tag the directory.\n\n### 4. The guard verifies this via `test_uses_evalconfig_allowed_scratch_roots_as_source_of_truth`, which narrows the allowlist to a single non-canonical entry and proves the guard follows.\n\n### 5. Exception chaining\n\n`raise ... from exc` is used at every check so `HomeContainmentViolation.__cause__` carries:\n\n- `InvalidEvalId` (with its own `eval_id` field, for forensic recovery of the offending string)\n- `ScratchRootViolation` (with `path`, `resolved`, `allowed` fields)\n- `FileNotFoundError` (raised by `Path.resolve(strict=True)`)\n\nReporters that walk the chain can render the underlying detail without parsing `HomeContainmentViolation.detail`.\n\n## Test scaffolding\n\n### `_materialize_home` helper\n\n`tests/cli/eval/test_path_containment.py:75` — creates a HOME the same way `HomeIsolation.setup` would, so the `Path.resolve(strict=True)` in check 3 succeeds.
